title: The Pagan outlook
summary: How the old faiths of Europe see life and the gods.

claims.text: The Pagan creeds grew from harsh lands and are practical: look after yourself and your people, take what is needed, and accept that the weak may not survive.
Their gods are pitiless and hard to predict, seldom evil in the Christian sense of Satan but seldom loving; Pagans tend to be fatalists who hope for a full life, a good death and songs after it.

title: The Hidden Children
summary: An origin tale shared by Verbena and Dreamspeakers.

claims.text: Verbena grandmothers tell of the Hidden Children as a reminder of the heritage the Verbena share with the Dreamspeakers.
In the tale, before humanity existed there were the Pure Ones, beings of heavenly energy, who gathered the elemental essences and gave people their form and flesh.

title: Baerwald
summary: A Pagan fief in the Black Forest.

claims.text: Sir Garland, a witch facing a heresy charge, fled through the realm of Spirit into the Black Forest, a wood said to house dark Fae and shapeshifters, and claimed a stretch of it.
Pagans gathered there as a refuge from persecution, and in 1317 Sir Garland declared the land a fief named Baerwald, an open insult to Rome and the Empire.
The Church attacked it again and again, yet its people held out and lived there for more than a century.

title: Lady Nightshade
summary: A great figure of the Verbena Tradition.

claims.text: Lady Nightshade is counted the greatest of the Verbena and played a central part in founding the Tradition and keeping it alive.
Lady Nightshade's story begins in Harrogate, England, at Midsummer of 1435.
